saints.name: St. George
saints.title: Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: The soldier-martyr of the early Church, honoured across East and West as a model of courage…
biography: George was a martyr who suffered at or near Lydda, called Diospolis, in Palestine, traditionally about 303 in the persecution of Diocletian. Nothing certain is known of his life beyond his martyrdom, yet pilgrims from the sixth century onward venerated his tomb at Lydda, and churches in Syria, Egypt, and the West already bore his name.

A decree of Pope Gelasius about 495 already numbered him among those saints 'whose names are justly reverenced among men, but whose actions are only known to God'. The dragon legend — the knight who frees a king's daughter and converts her city — appears no earlier than the twelfth century and was spread by the Golden Legend.

Honoured as a soldier-martyr, he was seen, crusaders believed, fighting beside them with St. Demetrius at Antioch in 1098, and became a patron of soldiers and of chivalry. When Edward III founded the Order of the Garter under his patronage about 1347, George became the patron of England, whose banner still bears his red cross.
saints.knownFor: His witness as a soldier-martyr and his patronage of soldiers and England.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain), 23 April
